target: Distinct browser counts in existing primary CTA disclosures

customReplacement.reason: Existing project-native cards, table, filters and charts fit the requested owner briefing.

contract.purpose: App Health helps product teams understand web traffic, intentional user actions, and application health across their projects.
contract.purposeSource: SaaS Maker catalog projects[app-health].presentation.directory.purposeContract, PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md; inspected 2026-10-02.
contract.canonicalPurpose: App Health helps product teams understand web traffic, intentional user actions, and application health across their projects.
contract.driftNote: Historical proof details in PRODUCT.md are not used as current release evidence.
contract.audience: Owner and product teams tracking portfolio activity, acquisition and health.
contract.job: Scan the 55-product completed-day briefing, then expand a project's primary CTAs to distinguish repeated events from distinct recognized browsers.
contract.thesis: Preserve the approved Daily briefing composition and add browser-count truth inside its existing action disclosure; reuse that disclosure on phone cards.
contract.system: Retain existing shadcn tokens, editorial metric rail, product ledger, system sans text and monospace event names. Native details/summary disclosure, 44px touch target, explicit browser/event labels, muted secondary qualification.
contract.signature: A dated portfolio briefing whose metric strip, breakout stories and ranked project ledger make the 55-product day scannable in two minutes.
contract.risk: Summing distinct browsers across CTAs would double-count overlap. Keep counts per named action, never infer people, preserve unavailable sampled counts and measured zeroes.
contract.qualityBar: Per-action event and browser counts are easy to distinguish at 390/768/1440 in both themes. Unavailable is not zero. Long event names wrap without horizontal page overflow. Existing metrics, source filters, health labels and product drilldowns retain their hierarchy.

hierarchy.observation: The existing completed-day metric rail and Every project ledger remain primary. Per-action browser counts appear only in a closed-by-default disclosure beneath the unchanged action total.

typography.observation: The first desktop pass broke benchmark_opened across lines. Widening Actions from 10 to 16 percent makes this name and its 17 events / 3 browsers line legible. Event names remain monospace; counts and qualifications use existing small sans tokens in both themes.

composition.observation: After reducing Top source and Responses widths, a first pass truncated Google. Grouping source name and share into one stacked child fixes that defect; the final 1440px view shows Google and its full share. Expanded CTA details increase row height deliberately; collapsed ledger remains compact.

identity.observation: Retains App Health sidebar, dated report, browser/event measurement vocabulary, health qualification and ranked project ledger from the approved Daily briefing. No new theme, artwork, font or generic component surface.

interaction.observation: Native details starts closed. Focus plus Enter opens the same action details on desktop and cards. Fixture browser checks verify measured 17 events / 3 browsers, sampled browser-unavailable state, and measured 0 events / 0 browsers; summary target is 44px with visible focus ring.

responsive.observation: Rendered 390/768/1440 in light and dark. Phone/tablet cards expose the same counts instead of losing the capability. The readability/overflow check passes at all six states; long names wrap and the source button retains its meaning.
